name: Port Arthur Historic Site
note: Heritage site: open-air convict penitentiary and village ruins, World Heritage listed, open daily from 9AM; the peninsula's main attraction.

name: Isle of the Dead (Port Arthur)
note: Historic island cemetery in Port Arthur bay, reached only on an escorted tour from the historic site (about 1 hour).

name: Point Puer Boys' Prison
note: Historic boys' prison site across the bay from Port Arthur, reached only on an escorted tour (about 2 hours, seasonal).

name: Port Arthur Ghost Tour
note: Operator-run evening lantern tour of the Port Arthur ruins (about 90 minutes); the place is the historic site, so this is an operator product.

name: Tasman Island
note: Offshore island in Tasman National Park seen from the water on a 3-hour eco cruise run by Tasman Island Cruises from Port Arthur; not landable, so an operator's route to a sight.

name: Coal Mines Historic Site
note: Heritage site: ruins of an 1833 convict coal mine on the peninsula's north-east, World Heritage listed, free to visit.

name: Tasmanian Devil Unzoo
note: Wildlife park at Taranna where free-roaming animals, including Tasmanian devils, can be seen and hand-fed; a paid attraction.

name: Eaglehawk Neck
note: Isthmus village and a gateway to the peninsula's coastal sights, with the Officers Quarters Museum and the site of the convict dog line.

name: Officers Quarters Museum
note: Museum in the 1832 officers' quarters at Eaglehawk Neck Historic Site, guarding the convict route to Port Arthur.

name: Tessellated Pavement
note: Natural rock formation: a flat shore platform split into block-like sections, at the northern end of Pirates Bay.

name: Tasman Arch
note: Natural sea arch on the Tasman Sea side of the Eaglehawk Neck section of Tasman National Park, reached by a short walk from a car park.

name: Devils Kitchen
note: Natural sea-carved trench at the Eaglehawk Neck section of Tasman National Park, with a lookout beside a car park.

name: Tasman Blowhole
note: Coastal blowhole on Blowhole Road in the Eaglehawk Neck section of Tasman National Park, a shorter alternative to Maingon Blowhole.

name: Fossil Bay Lookout
note: Coastal lookout over Fossil Bay in Tasman National Park, near the blowhole, where water is blown up as a spray.

name: Pirates Bay Lookout
note: Coastal lookout over Pirates Bay on the Arthur Highway, the easy viewpoint for the bay and the Tessellated Pavement.

name: Martin Cash's Lookout
note: Lookout reached by a long winding road off the Arthur Highway, with views over the peninsula's east coast.

name: Tasman National Park
note: National park protecting the Tasman Peninsula's sea cliffs, arches, caves and capes, with the Three Capes Track; a park destination.

name: Remarkable Cave
note: Sea cavern in Tasman National Park, shaped like the outline of Tasmania, viewed from a lookout 15 minutes' walk from Maingon Bay Lookout.

name: Maingon Bay Lookout
note: Lookout and trailhead in Tasman National Park for Remarkable Cave and Maingon Blowhole.

name: Maingon Blowhole
note: Coastal blowhole in Tasman National Park, a one-hour return walk from Maingon Bay Lookout over steep, sometimes slippery track.

name: Cape Raoul
note: Sea-cliff cape in Tasman National Park with a lookout at the end of a 14 km return track (about 5 hours).

name: Cape Hauy
note: Sea-cliff cape on the Three Capes Track in Tasman National Park, known for its dolerite spires and lookout.

name: Cape Pillar
note: Sea-cliff cape on the Three Capes Track in Tasman National Park, reached on the walk's middle days past the Blade.

name: Three Capes Track
note: Multi-day guided or self-guided walk of about 48 km along the Tasman Peninsula's cliffs, from Port Arthur to Fortescue Bay; a Great Short Walk-style multi-day track.

name: Fortescue Bay
note: Sheltered white-sand beach campground at the end of the Three Capes Track in Tasman National Park, popular for swimming and snorkelling.

name: Dunalley
note: Small town at the gateway to the Tasman Peninsula, with a bakery, a Victorian hotel and a distillery nearby.

name: Nubeena
note: Town at the centre of the Tasman Peninsula and the nearest base for the Coal Mines Historic Site.

name: Sorell
note: Largest town in the South East, with historic Georgian churches and the region's main supermarkets.

name: Sorell Community Market
note: Market held at Sorell Memorial Hall on the second Sunday of each month: handmade goods, fresh food and vintage; a recurring market, not a permanent venue.

name: Sorell Fruit Farm
note: Fruit farm on Pawleena Road offering fruit picking (October to April, 10AM to 4PM daily); a seasonal farm business.

name: Sorell Churches
note: Group of heritage churches in Sorell (St Thomas' Catholic, St George's Anglican, Scots Uniting); the Wikivoyage listing names them as architecture to see from outside.

name: Primrose Sands
note: Small shack beach town on the Southern Beaches, named by Wikivoyage among Tasmania's best small beaches.

name: Lewisham
note: Small shack community on the Southern Beaches with a beach named among the region's best small beaches.

name: Dodges Ferry
note: Regional centre of the Southern Beaches with a beach named among the region's best small beaches, a cafe and a bakery.

name: Carlton
note: Historic riverside village on the Southern Beaches, named by Wikivoyage as a historic stop.

name: Bay of Fires
note: Coastal bay of white beaches and orange lichen-stained granite on the north-east coast, a conservation area also called Larapuna; a regional destination.

name: Binalong Bay
note: Small village at the southern end of the Bay of Fires Conservation Area, with a pizza bar, pub and the start of Bay of Fires beach walks.

name: Swimcart Beach
note: White-sand beach in the Bay of Fires Conservation Area at the end of the 42 km Bay of Fires mountain-bike trail, with camping behind it.

name: Stumpys Bay
note: Beach and campground at Mount William National Park's northern end, the start of the coastal heath walks.

name: Mount William National Park
note: National park of coastal heathland, white beaches and orange granite at the north end of the Bay of Fires; a park destination.

name: Eddystone Point Lighthouse
note: Historic lighthouse at Eddystone Point on the north end of the Bay of Fires, near the reefs named as excellent dive sites.

name: Ansons Bay
note: Small settlement on Ansons Bay, the nearest town for Mount William National Park and a fishing spot for bream and bass.

name: wukalina Walk
note: Four-day guided walk through Larapuna / Bay of Fires, owned and led by Palawa (Tasmanian Aboriginal) guides; an operator-run walk.

name: Bay of Fires Lodge Walk
note: Guided beach-to-beach walk on the Bay of Fires coast with nights in a lodge above the sea; an operator-run walk.

name: St Helens
note: Largest town on the north-east coast, a base for the Bay of Fires and known for game fishing and crayfish.

name: St Helens Mountain Bike Trails
note: Network of mountain-bike trails around St Helens, including the 42 km Bay of Fires trail from the Blue Tier to Swimcart Beach.

name: Beerbarrel Beach
note: Remote beach reached on a one-hour return walk from St Helens Point Conservation Area.

name: Scamander
note: Small coastal town between Bicheno and St Helens on the East Coast, named by Wikivoyage as a stop.

name: Bicheno
note: Beachside town on the East Coast, a base for little penguins, the Gulch, Douglas-Apsley and Freycinet.

name: Little Penguins of Bicheno
note: Wildlife viewing: little penguins come ashore at Bicheno each night from September to January; seen on operator-led tours (about $20 per person).

name: Bicheno Blowhole
note: Coastal blowhole reached by a walking track south of the Gulch; unfenced, so take care in rough weather.

name: The Gulch
note: Fishing harbour and rocky inlet at the south end of Bicheno, with a glass-bottom boat, a seafood cafe and a small aquarium.

name: Diamond Island
note: Small island off Bicheno reached on foot at low tide, with clear rock pools and a penguin sanctuary.

name: Governor Island Marine Reserve
note: Marine reserve just off Bicheno with kelp reefs and sponge gardens, one of Australia's best temperate diving sites; a dive and snorkel area.

name: Whalers' Lookout
note: Lookout reached by a walk above Bicheno, named by Wikivoyage as a short walk to take.

name: Waubedebar's Grave
note: Grave marker of the Aboriginal leader Waubedebar in Bicheno, a minor memorial.

name: Bicheno Motorcycle Museum
note: Private museum on Burgess Street with over 60 restored motorcycles on display, open 9AM to 5PM.

name: East Coast Natureworld
note: Wildlife park on Bicheno's outskirts with daily Tasmanian devil feeding presentations and hand-feeding of free-ranging animals; a paid attraction.

name: Lobster Shack Bicheno
note: Waterfront seafood cafe above the rocks of the Gulch fishing harbour; a restaurant, listed for its seafood.

name: Douglas-Apsley National Park
note: National park of dry eucalypt forest, gorges and swimming waterholes on the Douglas and Apsley rivers, 15 minutes west of Bicheno; a park destination.

name: Apsley Waterhole
note: Large swimming pool on the Apsley River reached by a 15-minute return walk from the park's only car park; the park's main day-visit swim.

name: Apsley Gorge
note: Rocky gorge in Douglas-Apsley National Park with plunge pools, reached by a 7 km loop walk of 4 to 5 hours.

name: Freycinet National Park
note: National park of granite peaks (The Hazards) and white beaches, including Wineglass Bay; a flagship park destination.

name: Wineglass Bay
note: Crescent of white sand within Freycinet National Park, reached by a 3-hour walk over the hills from the car park.

name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
note: Lookout over Wineglass Bay, a shorter well-formed walk from the same car park, with the classic view of the bay.

name: Mount Amos
note: Summit walk in Freycinet National Park with views over Wineglass Bay, a medium walk of 2 to 4 hours return.

name: The Hazards
note: Pink granite mountain range at the centre of Freycinet National Park, seen from Coles Bay and the park road; a viewed landscape feature.

name: Cape Tourville Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse on a boardwalked cliff track at the end of a 6.4 km sealed road in Freycinet National Park, with sweeping coastal views.

name: Friendly Beaches
note: Long white-sand beaches on the north-east side of Freycinet National Park, reached by gravel roads and foot tracks from the Coles Bay Road.

name: Honeymoon Bay
note: Quieter bay in Freycinet National Park with a campground, named by Wikivoyage for snorkelling and diving; an alternative to Wineglass Bay.

name: Sleepy Bay
note: Short walk to a bay in Freycinet National Park, named for snorkelling and diving.

name: Little Gravelly Beach
note: Short walk to a beach in Freycinet National Park, one of the park's under-two-hour walks.

name: Hazards Beach
note: Long walk to a beach in Freycinet National Park, part of the 4 to 8 hour Wineglass Bay and Hazards Beach circuit.

name: Saltwater Lagoon
note: Short walk to a lagoon on the Friendly Beaches in Freycinet National Park.

name: Freycinet Experience Walk
note: Four-day lodge-based walk of 33 to 37 km along the Freycinet Peninsula, run by a private operator; an operator product.

name: Coles Bay
note: Small seaside town at the foot of the Hazards, the main service centre for Freycinet National Park.

name: Freycinet Marine Farm
note: Oyster and seafood marine farm on Great Oyster Bay with a farm-gate sales outlet and covered seating; a venue for oysters.

name: Melshell Oysters
note: Oyster lease and tasting venue on the Freycinet Peninsula; a food venue.

name: Sail Freycinet
note: Sailing and cruise operator at Coles Bay; an operator product, the sea around Freycinet is the place.

name: Oyster Bay Tours
note: Tour operator running oyster-farm tours and tastings from Coles Bay; an operator product.

name: Spring Beach
note: White-sand beach on the Great Eastern Drive south of Triabunna, with a clifftop walk from Shelly Beach through an old sandstone quarry.

name: Swansea
note: Seaside village on Great Oyster Bay, overlooking the Hazards, with a local history museum and a base for the east coast's food and wine.

name: East Coast Heritage Museum
note: Local history museum on Franklin Street in Swansea, open daily 10AM to 4PM with a gold-coin donation.

name: Morris General Store
note: Historic general store in Swansea, a shop listed under See; a shop, not a sight.

name: Spring Vale Vineyard
note: Vineyard and cellar door at Cranbrook on the East Coast Wine Trail, in a stable built by convicts in 1842; a winery.

name: Milton Vineyard
note: Vineyard near Swansea, named as the wine partner to the town's oysters; a winery.

name: Kate's Berry Farm
note: Berry farm south of Swansea with fresh berries, chocolates and berry wine; a farm business.

name: Bangor Vineyard
note: Vineyard at Dunalley with attached restaurant and wine tasting; a winery.

name: Dunalley Bay Distillery
note: Distillery on the shores of Dunalley Bay with tastings; a distillery.

name: McHenry Distillery
note: Distillery on the slopes of Mount Arthur above Port Arthur with tastings and gin workshops; a distillery.

name: Triabunna
note: Small town and the ferry gateway for Maria Island, with the Maria Island ferry and east coast cruise operators.

name: Maria Island National Park
note: Island national park reached only by ferry from Triabunna: convict-era ruins, cliffs, walks and wildlife; a park destination.

name: Darlington Probation Station
note: Convict probation station ruins at Darlington on Maria Island, a World Heritage Australian Convict Site; the island's main settlement and visitor hub.

name: Fossil Cliffs
note: Cliffs on Maria Island with many fossils, reached by a 4.5 km circuit of 1.5 to 2.5 hours from Darlington.

name: Painted Cliffs
note: Sandstone cliffs on Maria Island with natural colour and swirl patterns, seen from the rock platform within two hours of low tide.

name: Maria Island Marine Reserve
note: Marine reserve around Maria Island used for swimming, snorkelling and rock pool exploring; a water area.

name: Orford
note: Holiday village at the mouth of the Prosser River, a base for Maria Island and the start of the Great Eastern Drive.

name: Stapleton Beach
note: Swimming beach at Orford linked by a 2 km coastal walk with Spring and Shelly beaches.

name: Shelly Beach
note: Swimming beach at Orford on the coastal walk to Spring Beach.

name: Raspins Beach
note: Conservation-area beach north of the Prosser River at Orford, a swimming beach and birdwatching spot.

name: Orford Bird Sanctuary
note: Bird sanctuary at Orford where fairy terns can be seen; a wildlife viewing area.

name: Paradise Probation Station
note: Convict probation station ruins reached on the convict road along the Prosser River from Orford.

name: Oatlands
note: Historic village on Lake Dulverton with about 150 sandstone Georgian buildings, mostly convict-built, on the Midland Highway.

name: Callington Mill
note: Australia's third-oldest windmill (1837) in Oatlands, now the centrepiece of Callington Mill Distillery.

name: Lake Dulverton
note: Lake on the edge of Oatlands with half-submerged cow sculptures and a 7 km walking trail to Parattah.

name: Oatlands Supreme Court
note: Courthouse built in 1829 in Oatlands, one of the town's heritage buildings, visited on the Oatlands Key entry to historic sites.

name: Ross
note: Georgian sandstone village on the Heritage Highway with many of Tasmania's oldest buildings and one of its oldest bridges.

name: Ross Female Factory
note: Convict women's prison site in Ross, a heritage site open to visitors.

name: Ross Bridge
note: Sandstone bridge built by convicts in 1836 on the Roseneath Road in Ross, one of Australia's oldest bridges, with a barbecue and resting spot.

name: Tasmanian Wool Centre Museum
note: Museum on Church Street in Ross about Tasmanian wool production, open daily.

name: Campbell Town
note: Midlands town on the Heritage Highway at the junction with the A4 to the east coast, a stop with a museum and parks.

name: Heritage Highway Museum
note: Local history museum in Campbell Town's town hall, free to enter, open Monday to Friday 10AM to 3PM.

name: Campbell Town Red Bridge
note: Red-painted bridge in Campbell Town, seen from Blackburn Park; a photo stop.

name: Campbell Town Agricultural Show
note: Annual two-day agricultural show held in early June, founded in 1838; an annual event, not a permanent place.

name: Richmond
note: Intact colonial town on the Heritage Highway with over 50 Georgian buildings, a day trip from Hobart.

name: Richmond Bridge
note: Convict-built sandstone bridge over the Coal River, built in 1823 and claimed as Australia's oldest bridge; a photo stop.

name: Richmond Gaol
note: Australia's oldest convict gaol, operating 1825 to 1840, part of the Richmond Gaol Historic Site managed by Parks and Wildlife.

name: Old Hobart Town
note: Miniature model village in Richmond showing Hobart as it stood in the 1820s; a paid attraction.

name: Pooseum
note: Quirky science museum in Richmond about animal droppings and digestion; a paid attraction for families.

name: Richmond Maze
note: Hedge labyrinth on Richmond Bridge Road with games and food, a paid family attraction.
